Nigeria will be under pressure to secure a crucial victory when they face Tanzania in Tuesday’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier, with the hosts equally desperate to end their winless run in the competition, PUNCH Sports Extra reports. While Tanzania have already secured qualification for the finals as co-hosts, the Super Eagles need all three points to boost their chances of reaching the tournament, which will be staged in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda from June 19 to July 17, 2027. Nigeria revived their campaign with a 3-1 victory over the Taifa Stars in Friday’s first leg at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo. Alhassan Yusuf opened the scoring within two minutes, before substitute Tolu Arokodare struck twice in the second half. The win lifted Eric Chelle’s side to six points from three matches, one behind Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau, who drew 1-1 with Madagascar on Friday. With Tanzania already assured of a place at the finals, only the best-placed team among the remaining three countries in Group L will qualify. A victory in Zanzibar would therefore take Nigeria temporarily to the top of the group, ahead of Guinea-Bissau’s later meeting with Madagascar. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Their 3-0 loss to Guinea-Bissau in September also underlines the need for greater consistency on the road. For Tanzania, Tuesday’s encounter offers an opportunity to claim their first victory of the qualifying campaign, even though the result will not affect their place at the finals. Miguel Angel Gamondi’s side were competitive in the first half of Friday’s meeting in Uyo but faded after the break, allowing Nigeria to take control and secure a comfortable victory. The Taifa Stars have struggled for results in recent months, winning just one of their last 16 matches across all competitions. They are also without a competitive home victory since being awarded a 3-0 win over Congo in March 2025. Tanzania will also be hoping to end their poor record against Nigeria. The two sides have met nine times, with the Super Eagles winning six and drawing three, leaving the Taifa Stars still searching for their first victory in the fixture. With Nigeria chasing a vital result and Tanzania eager to give their supporters something to celebrate, Tuesday’s encounter promises to be a contest of contrasting motivations Abiodun Adewale Abiodun, who reports Sports for PUNCH, covers different tiers of the Nigerian football league, the national teams, as well as cricket, in the last six years
